Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:13:1.english: To his garden or to his ruin, from where [is it derived] - that it is [considered a valid] return and he is exempt [from further responsibility].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:14:1.english: The owner’s knowledge - To say to him, “Watch your cow, for I have returned it to your garden, as I found it lost.”

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:14:2.hebrew: הכל צריך דעת בעלים - גנב, גזלן וד' שומרים שהשיבו, צריכין להודיעו. ואם לא הודיעו ומתה או נגנבה, חייבים באחריותן, דכיון דידע שאבדה ולא ידע שהושבה, לא נזהר בה ולא מאכילה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:14:2.english: All [returns] require the owner’s knowledge - A thief, a robber, and the four [types of] bailees who returned [an animal] must inform [the owner]. And if they did not inform him, and it died or was stolen, they bear liability for it, because since he knew that it was lost and did not know that it had been returned, he does not guard it and does not feed it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:15:1.english: Send away - Regarding sending away [the mother bird from] the nest.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:15:2.hebrew: תרתי זמני - ואנן תנן: שלחה וחזרה, שלחה וחזרה, אפילו ארבע וה' פעמים חייב:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:15:2.english: Twice - Yet we learned [in a Mishnah]: [If] he sent it away and it returned, sent it away and it returned, even four or five times, he is obligated [to send it away].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:16:1.english: For an optional matter - [Meaning] that he does not need the bird except to eat it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:16:2.hebrew: לדבר מצוה מנין - היה צריך לטהר בו את המצורע, מנין שאסור באם על הבנים? ת"ל: תשלח:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:16:2.english: For a matter involving a mitzva, from where [is it derived] - [If] one needed [the bird] to purify a leper with it, from where [do we know] that he is prohibited from [taking] the mother with the young? The verse states: "Teshallaḥ" [you shall send away].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:19:1.english: You shall surely release [it] - [This refers to] unloading.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:1:1.english: Isratiyya [a main thoroughfare] - A beaten road for the public.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:1:2.english: That is flowing and coming - Toward his fellow's field.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:20:1.english: You shall surely lift [it] up - [This refers to] loading.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:21:1.english: Monetary loss - For the animal is damaged.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:22:1.hebrew: משום דבשכר - שנותנין לו שכר, דאיכא למ"ד לקמן (בבא מציעא דף לב.) טעינה בשכר, פריקה בחנם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:22:1.english: Due to [the fact] that [it is] with remuneration - [Meaning] that they give him wages, for there is one who says later (Bava Metzia 32a): loading is for pay, [and] unloading is for free.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:23:1.hebrew: לא מסיימי קראי - הי משמע טעינה והי משמע פריקה. ואי כתב חדא, הוה אמינא לפריקה אתא, אבל טעינה לא; כתב רחמנא אידך לטעינה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:23:1.english: The verses are not clearly defined - [as to] which implies loading and which implies unloading. And if [the Torah] had written [only] one, I would have said [that] it comes for unloading, but loading [is] not [obligated]; [therefore] the Merciful One wrote the other [verse] for loading.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:24:1.hebrew: למה לי למכתב אבידה - השבת אבידה. לכתוב או הא או הא וליגמר מניה, דהא כולהו אזהרות ממון ישראל הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:24:1.english: Why do I [need the Torah] to write a lost item - [Meaning,] returning a lost item. Let [the Torah] write either this or that and derive [the other] from it, for all of them are warnings [regarding] a Jew's property.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:24:2.hebrew: צערא דמרה - הוא העומד שם ואין יכול לטעון לבדו, וכן לפרוק:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:24:2.english: The suffering of its owner - He is the one standing there and cannot load [it] by himself, and likewise to unload [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:24:3.english: That its owner is not with it - [such] that he would trouble himself to return it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:2:1.english: Rava said: “With every lost item,” etc. - It is an independent statement that Rava said in the study hall.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:3:1.hebrew: מאי למימרא - ותיפוק ליה משום עומרין שישנן בכלל אבידה, דדמו לפרטא דשה ושלמה, ולמה לי לכל לרבוינהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:3:1.english: What [is the need] to state [it] - Let it be derived [from the fact that there are] sheaves, which are included in [the category of] a lost item, since they resemble the specific examples of a sheep and a garment; so why do I need [the word] "for every" to include them?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:5:1.hebrew: רועה בדרך - איכא תרתי למעליותא: חדא דרועה, ועוד דאפילו רצה לא מסתקבא. רצה בין הכרמים, איכא תרתי לגריעותא: חדא דרצה, ועוד דכרמים מסקבי לה. רצה בדרך, איכא חדא לגריעותא: דרצה ומתקלקלת בריצתה, אי נמי תלך למרחקים. רועה בין הכרמים, חדא לגריעותא: דזימנין דמסתקבא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:5:1.english: Grazing on the path - There are two favorable factors: one, that it is grazing; and furthermore, that even if it were running, it would not be injured. [In the case of] running among the vineyards, there are two unfavorable factors: one, that it is running; and furthermore, that the vineyards injure it. [In the case of] running on the path, there is one unfavorable factor: that it is running and becomes harmed by its running, or else it will go far away. [In the case of] grazing among the vineyards, [there is] one unfavorable factor: that at times it is injured.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:8:1.english: And this [is] with regard to the loss of [the animal] itself, etc. - [The Gemara] goes on to explain it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 31a:8:2.english: With regard to loss of land - And one is obligated to remove it because of the damage to vineyards.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 31a:1:1.hebrew: קורדום בצד גדר - פירשתי לעיל (בבא מציעא כה: סד"ה ואם נטל):
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 31a:1:1.english: An ax alongside a fence - I explained [this] above (Bava Metzia 25b, end of s.v. "Ve'im natal"):

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 31a:21:1.hebrew: למה לי למכתב רחמנא פריקה כו' - אין לפרש "למה לי דכתב כוליה קרא דפריקה או דטעינה", דא"כ היכי קאמר "אי אשמועינן טעינה דבשכר"? הא משמע לקמן (בבא מציעא דף לב.) דטעינה לא הוי בשכר אלא משום דנכתב פריקה! ועוד, דלא שייכא הך צריכותא אלא לקמן. אלא י"ל: למה לי דכתב רחמנא יתורא דמרבינן "אין בעליו עמו" בפריקה, ולמה לי דכתב בטעינה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 31a:21:1.english: "Why did the Merciful One [need] to write unloading, etc." - One should not explain [this as], "Why did [Scripture] write the entire verse of unloading or of loading?" For if so, how could [the Gemara] say, "If [it] had taught us [only] loading, [which is] for pay"? Why, it is implied later (Bava Metzia 32a) that loading is not for pay except because unloading was written! And furthermore, that tzerikhuta [explanation of why both verses are needed] is only relevant later. Rather, one must say [that the Gemara means]: Why did the Merciful One write the extra [phrase] from which we include [the case where] "its owner is not with it" regarding unloading, and why did He write [it] regarding loading?

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 31a:23:1.hebrew: לרבי שמעון לא מסיימי קראי - תימה, דלקמן (בבא מציעא דף לב.) משמע דקרא ד"נופלים בדרך" לא מסיים לר"ש דהוי בטעינה, ד"טעונייהו עלייהו" משמע, ואי לא כתב אלא חד הוה מוקמי ליה בפריקה, אבל קרא ד"רובץ תחת משאו" לא משמע לכ"ע אלא בפריקה; וכשנכתבו שניהם, ע"כ גם לר"ש קרא ד"נופלים בדרך" הוי בטעינה, וא"כ לר"ש לא יכתוב אלא חד יתורא ל"אין בעליו עמו" בקרא ד"נופלים בדרך". וי"ל, ד"רובץ תחת משאו" נמי לא מסיים לר"ש, דאפשר למשמע בטעינה, דע"י שאין הרבה בני אדם לטעון מכביד המשוי על הבהמה ורובצת; ולקמן לא אצטריך למימר דלא מסיימי אלא אקרא ד"נופלים בדרך". והא דפריך לקמן (בבא מציעא דף לב:): "והא 'וחדלת' בפריקה הוא דכתיב" — לא הוי אלא אליבא דרבנן, דלר"ש מצי למהוי בטעינה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 31a:23:1.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, the verses are not clearly defined - This is puzzling, for later (Bava Metzia 32a) it is implied that [only] the verse of "falling on the road" is not clearly defined according to Rabbi Shimon as referring to loading — since it implies [that] their loads are upon them, and if [Scripture] had written only one [verse], they would have established it as referring to unloading — whereas the verse of "crouching under its burden" implies according to everyone only unloading. And when both of them are written, perforce even according to Rabbi Shimon the verse of "falling on the road" refers to loading; and if so, according to Rabbi Shimon, [Scripture] should have written only one superfluous [expression] for [the case where] its owner is not with it, in the verse of "falling on the road." And one can answer that "crouching under its burden" is also not clearly defined according to Rabbi Shimon, for it is possible to understand [it as referring] to loading, since because there are not many people to load [it], the burden weighs heavily upon the animal and it crouches. And later, [the Gemara] only needed to say that it is not clearly defined with respect to the verse of "falling on the road." And that which [the Gemara] asks later (Bava Metzia 32b): "But 'and you shall refrain' is written regarding unloading!" — that is only according to the Rabbis, for according to Rabbi Shimon it can refer to loading.
